newsitem.title: THAILAND: Jailed Briton allowed to leave Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Briton allowed to leave Thailand.

text.p: A British woman who was sentenced to 25 years in prison for trying to smuggle heroin out of Thailand won approval on Thursday to serve the remainder of her sentence in Britain, a Thai official said.
A special 10-member committee agreed to a request by Sandra Gregory to extradite her to her home country, Kukiat Sunthornbura, permanent secretary of the Justice Ministry, told Reuters.
He said Gregory, 31, from Halifax, northern England, had already served four years and two months of her sentence.
"The next process is for officials of the Thai corrections department and the police to determine how to send her back," he said.

Under Thai law, a foreign prisoner who has served a certain amount of timne in Thailand can apply to be sent home to serve the rest of the sentence. The number of years varies according to the charges.
The appeal to return home was made on Gregory's behalf by the British Embassy, court documents showed.
In February 1996, Gregory was sentenced to 25 years in jail for heroin smuggling. An original death sentence was commuted because she had confessed.
Gregory was detained along with Robert Lock, from Cambridge, in February 1993 as they were about to board a flight to Japan.
She was found with 102 grams (3.6 ounces) of heroin in her possession.
Gregory pleaded guilty but told the court Lock had paid her to smuggle the heroin out of Thailand. Lock was found not guilty in last year's hearing.
